task.title: Slice 1 of #14918: establish serve-proxy transport legs

issue.title: id: complete serve-proxy protocol after codec and mux-credit slices

slice.criterion: A TLS 1.3/HTTP CONNECT leg and the optional WebSocket binary-message adapter both establish a transport that carries the same typed serve-proxy frames.

payload.problem: Issue #7569 closed after codec slice PR #7666 while explicitly listing the remaining serve-proxy protocol work. PR #13859 adds mux credit accounting but says no live leg is wired. The first prerequisite is the TLS/CONNECT + WebSocket leg that carries the existing typed frames.
evidence: PR #7666 body says it implements slice 1 only and lists leg establishment, mux routing/scheduling, keepalive, resumption and E2E ciphertext forwarding as remaining.
PR #13859 body confirms the mux credit consumer exists but is not wired into a live leg.
Issue #7569 and design #5792 define the full protocol; the closure-review pointer is on issue #13871.
acceptance: A TLS 1.3 TCP leg can use HTTP CONNECT and exchange typed frames through the established serve-proxy codec.
The optional WebSocket binary-message adapter carries the same typed frames where CONNECT is unavailable.
Named-oracle transport tests cover frame round-trip for each supported leg and reject malformed/oversized frames at the boundary.
The implementation leaves #5792 trust and E2E invariants unchanged.

include: Focused transport tests for typed frame exchange
exclude: Mux stream-ID mapping and priority scheduling
Resume tokens and replay state machine

tests: Add a focused test whose oracle is typed-frame byte preservation across each transport adapter and the 16 KiB DATA cap; run the focused id serve-proxy leg test through CI/Fleet.
payload.priority_reason: First prerequisite slice for an explicitly incomplete security-sensitive broker protocol; it adds transport establishment without changing trust or payload semantics.

dedupe.basis: No live queued task for issue #7569/serve-proxy remaining slices was found. The open issue search contains no leg-establishment follow-up; #13859 covers only mux credit accounting.
